_meta.caveats: General information, not legal advice. State laws change often; verify the current statute before acting. Rent withholding and repair-and-deduct are risky: tenants who use them wrongly can be evicted, so follow notice steps exactly and keep records. Many big cities add stronger rules: New York City (HPD entry and repair rules, rent stabilization), San Francisco and Los Angeles (rent ordinances, deposit interest), Chicago (RLTO: 2-day entry notice, deposit interest, repair-and-deduct, withholding), Seattle (deposit and move-in fee limits), Washington DC (rent control), Portland OR and Montgomery County MD. Kentucky and Tennessee remedies apply only in areas that adopted the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act. Penalties usually require the landlord to have acted in bad faith or willfully. Puerto Rico data is thin and largely unverified. The url field points to the state's code on Justia; check the specific statute there.
